newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti shares tumble on results worries.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti shares tumble on results worries.

text.p: Shares in Italy's Olivetti tumbled on Tuesday with investors fearing the worst from preliminary 1996 group results due late on Wednesday which could include huge write-down and restructuring charges.

Shares in the information and technology group slumped almost seven percent before settling off 1.81 percent at 645 lire around 1400 GMT as the market feared net 1996 losses could amount to 900 billion lire ($560 million) or even more for 1996.
"The market is focusing on how much Olivetti will attempt to clean up its balance sheet," said one industry analyst in Milan.
Olivetti is expected to issue figures on 1996 revenue, end-1996 debt levels and indications of profitability after its first board meeting of 1997 to be held on Wednesday.

Analysts say the key issue is by how much Olivetti decides to write down the value of its international holdings and clean up its balance sheet, and how severe will be restructuring charges across its businesses.

Olivetti has not made a profit since 1990 as it struggled with a loss-making personal computer business, whose sale it announced last week to a consortium of investors grouped together in Piedmont International.

Analysts expect Olivetti's two developing sectors -- mobile phone consortium Omnitel and fixed-line telecoms company Telemedia -- to be still in loss as in the first half, since it is still investing in these newly-started businesses.
But there are worries over Olivetti Solutions, formerly Systems and Services, and Lexikon office equipment, both in profit in the first half but suffering profits squeezes.
"There has been talk that Olivetti Solutions, which is still the core of the whole business, may have slipped into loss for 1996 which is causing some unease," said another Milan analyst.

The company's debt was put at 2.916 trillion lire at end-November, and it is set to announce a December debt figure on Wednesday. The debt level is seen falling rapidly when money comes in from sell-offs since Roberto Colaninno took over as group chief executive in September.

The sales of a 5.6 percent stake in Omnitel for 432.5 billion lire and the personal computer company for 250-300 billion lire are expected almost to match predictions contained in Colaninno's restructuring plan.
A partial float of the Lexikon business late in 1997 is seen raising most of the 400 billion lire of the plan for 1997.

In 1995, the group turned in a net loss of 1.589 trillion lire after restructuring charges of 1.123 trillion lire, but at the operating level it made a 114 billion lire profit despite some 200 billion lire of losses at PCs.
But in the first half of 1996, results showed the group slipped into an operating loss of 81 billion lire and pretax profit slumped to 440.2 billion lire. ($1=1,611 lire)
